# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✋ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤙 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟 👍 🤙 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I see the bomb’s visible data but cannot read the manual or touch it. I am telling Blind the display, light, and wire colours directly. I am also establishing a fixed gesture code with Mute so that future tactile or manual information can reach me reliably; Mute should give the manual’s instructions to Blind verbally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot hear speech. The visible facts are: display 3; light green; wire 1 red; wire 2 green; wire 3 blue. Establish this reporting code for messages to Deaf: 👍 means display, 👎 means light, 👌 means wire 1, ☝ means wire 2, ✌ means wire 3, 🤟 means tactile or other report. For values, 🖐 means red, ✋ means green, 👆 means blue, 👇 means white, 👈 means yellow, 👉 means black. Use the digit gestures as follows: 🤛 zero, 🤜 one, ✊ two, 👊 three, 👋 four, 🤚 five, 🖖 six, 🤌 seven, 🤏 eight, 🤞 nine. Please tell Blind the manual’s required procedure and use this code to relay any remaining information to me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb facts: display 3; light green; wire 1 red; wire 2 green; wire 3 blue. Mute has the manual and will tell you its required procedure. Do not act until the manual and your tactile observations agree.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 👎 ✋ 👌 🖐 ☝ ✋ ✌ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌 🖐]

Mute’s gestures decode to a confirmation of the visible facts: display 3, green light, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. The second message specifically repeats that wire 1 is red. No manual instruction has reached me yet, so I am directing Mute to give the manual’s exact procedure to Blind, while warning Blind not to act on the colour data alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded report confirms: display 3, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. No manual procedure has reached me yet. Wait for Mute's exact instructions before touching or cutting anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact procedure directly to Blind now, including the required action and any ordering or confirmation rules. Do not rely on gestures for instructions.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 👎 ✋ 🤟 🖐 👌]

The new coded message decodes as: display 3, light green, an additional “tactile/other” report marked red, and wire 1. It does not provide an actionable procedure. I am again directing Mute to relay the manual verbatim to Blind, who is the only one able to perform the procedure.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your coded message is not an actionable manual instruction. Speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind now, including what part to operate, which wire or colour matters, and any required sequence. Do not send only gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="I still have no reliable manual procedure. Do not operate the bomb yet. Ask Mute for the manual's exact instructions and report your tactile findings to Mute.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤛 🤛 🤛 👎 ✋ 👌 🖐 ☝ ✋ ✌ 👆 🤟 👌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤞]

Mute’s message again encodes the visible values, with the display apparently represented as three zeroes, followed by light green and the three wire colours; it still contains no manual procedure. Blind’s gestures are not part of the agreed code, so I cannot safely interpret them. I am explicitly routing the manual request to Mute and telling Blind to obtain and follow it before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your latest message still gives only display, light, and wire data; it does not convey the manual procedure. Speak the manual's exact instructions aloud to Blind now. Blind must know precisely what to operate, which wire or setting to use, and in what order.")
speak(to="blind", text="I cannot safely decode your gestures because they are outside our agreed code. Mute still has not relayed the manual procedure. Please ask Mute aloud for the exact procedure, then report your tactile findings to Mute before acting.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌 🖐]

The latest message decodes under our established code as “tactile/other — wire 1 — red.” Since Mute cannot speak, this is the only manual-related report reaching me. I will pass the wire identification to Blind, but I will not claim that cutting or operating it is safe without a clear manual instruction and Blind’s tactile confirmation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest coded report is: tactile or other information; wire 1; red. The visible bomb also shows wire 1 red, display 3, and green light. Please identify wire 1 by touch and report whether the manual indicates an action on it before operating anything.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute’s latest coded signal is ☝, which our agreed code means “wire 2.” I am relaying that as the manual-related selection, while distinguishing it from the visible colour facts. Blind should verify the second wire by touch and use the manual’s procedure rather than acting on my interpretation alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest coded signal means wire 2. The visible facts remain: display 3, green light, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Verify the second wire by touch and apply the manual's procedure to it; do not act if your tactile findings or the manual disagree.")
```
